reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 3 AUR repository files (PKGBUILD, .gitignore, .SRCINFO). The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe: standard binary packaging with pinned checksums from official GitHub releases, no dangerous commands, no .install hooks. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' result was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing .SRCINFO, not a security finding. The qwen model did successfully audit PKGBUILD and .gitignore as safe. Since the only disagreement stems from a tool error rather than a security concern, and the complete audit found no injection patterns, the package is safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when attempting to audit .SRCINFO. This is a tool failure, not a security finding. learnings: API errors on individual files should not cause the entire audit to be marked inconclusive when other files were successfully reviewed; the tool should aggregate partial results
